ShaderNodeAmbientOcclusion.name: Ambient Occlusion
ShaderNodeAmbientOcclusion.bl_description:
Compute how much the hemisphere above the shading point is occluded, for example to add weathering effects to corners.
Note: For Cycles, this may slow down renders significantly

ShaderNodeAttribute.name: Attribute
ShaderNodeAttribute.bl_description: Retrieve attributes attached to objects or geometry

ShaderNodeBackground.name: Background
ShaderNodeBackground.bl_description:
Add background light emission.
Note: This node should only be used for the world surface output

ShaderNodeBevel.name: Bevel
ShaderNodeBevel.bl_description:
Generates normals with round corners.
Note: only supported in Cycles, and may slow down renders

ShaderNodeBlackbody.name: Blackbody
ShaderNodeBlackbody.bl_description: Convert a blackbody temperature to an RGB value

ShaderNodeBrightContrast.name: Brightness/Contrast
ShaderNodeBrightContrast.bl_description: Control the brightness and contrast of the input color

ShaderNodeBsdfAnisotropic.name: Glossy BSDF
ShaderNodeBsdfAnisotropic.bl_description: Reflection with microfacet distribution, used for materials such as metal or mirrors

ShaderNodeBsdfGlass.name: Glass BSDF
ShaderNodeBsdfGlass.bl_description: Glass-like shader mixing refraction and reflection at grazing angles

ShaderNodeBsdfHair.name: Hair BSDF
ShaderNodeBsdfHair.bl_description: Reflection and transmission shaders optimized for hair rendering

ShaderNodeBsdfHairPrincipled.name: Principled Hair BSDF
ShaderNodeBsdfHairPrincipled.bl_description: Physically-based, easy-to-use shader for rendering hair and fur

ShaderNodeBsdfMetallic.name: Metallic BSDF
ShaderNodeBsdfMetallic.bl_description: Metallic reflection with microfacet distribution, and metallic fresnel

ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled.name: Principled BSDF
ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled.bl_description: Physically-based, easy-to-use shader for rendering surface materials, based on the OpenPBR model

ShaderNodeBsdfRayPortal.name: Ray Portal BSDF
ShaderNodeBsdfRayPortal.bl_description: Continue tracing from an arbitrary new position and in a new direction

ShaderNodeBsdfRefraction.name: Refraction BSDF
ShaderNodeBsdfRefraction.bl_description: Glossy refraction with sharp or microfacet distribution, typically used for materials that transmit light

ShaderNodeBsdfSheen.name: Sheen BSDF
ShaderNodeBsdfSheen.bl_description:
Reflection for materials such as cloth.
Typically mixed with other shaders (such as a Diffuse Shader) and is not particularly useful on its own

ShaderNodeBsdfToon.name: Toon BSDF
ShaderNodeBsdfToon.bl_description: Diffuse and Glossy shaders with cartoon light effects

ShaderNodeBsdfTransparent.name: Transparent BSDF
ShaderNodeBsdfTransparent.bl_description: Transparency without refraction, passing straight through the surface as if there were no geometry

ShaderNodeBump.name: Bump
ShaderNodeBump.bl_description: Generate a perturbed normal from a height texture for bump mapping. Typically used for faking highly detailed surfaces

ShaderNodeCameraData.name: Camera Data
ShaderNodeCameraData.bl_description: Retrieve information about the camera and how it relates to the current shading point's position

ShaderNodeClamp.name: Clamp
ShaderNodeClamp.bl_description: Clamp a value between a minimum and a maximum

ShaderNodeCombineColor.name: Combine Color
ShaderNodeCombineColor.bl_description: Create a color from individual components using multiple models

ShaderNodeCombineXYZ.name: Combine XYZ
ShaderNodeCombineXYZ.bl_description: Create a vector from X, Y, and Z components

ShaderNodeDisplacement.name: Displacement
ShaderNodeDisplacement.bl_description: Displace the surface along the surface normal

ShaderNodeEeveeSpecular.name: Specular BSDF
ShaderNodeEeveeSpecular.bl_description: Similar to the Principled BSDF node but uses the specular workflow instead of metallic, which functions by specifying the facing (along normal) reflection color. Energy is not conserved, so the result may not be physically accurate

ShaderNodeFloatCurve.name: Float Curve
ShaderNodeFloatCurve.bl_description: Map an input float to a curve and outputs a float value

ShaderNodeFresnel.name: Fresnel
ShaderNodeFresnel.bl_description:
Produce a blending factor depending on the angle between the surface normal and the view direction using Fresnel equations.
Typically used for mixing reflections at grazing angles

ShaderNodeHoldout.name: Holdout
ShaderNodeHoldout.bl_description:
Create a "hole" in the image with zero alpha transparency, which is useful for compositing.
Note: the holdout shader can only create alpha when transparency is enabled in the film settings

ShaderNodeHueSaturation.name: Hue/Saturation/Value
ShaderNodeHueSaturation.bl_description: Apply a color transformation in the HSV color model

ShaderNodeInvert.name: Invert Color
ShaderNodeInvert.bl_description: Invert a color, producing a negative

ShaderNodeLayerWeight.name: Layer Weight
ShaderNodeLayerWeight.bl_description:
Produce a blending factor depending on the angle between the surface normal and the view direction.
Typically used for layering shaders with the Mix Shader node

ShaderNodeLightFalloff.name: Light Falloff
ShaderNodeLightFalloff.bl_description: Manipulate how light intensity decreases over distance. Typically used for non-physically-based effects; in reality light always falls off quadratically

ShaderNodeLightPath.name: Light Path
ShaderNodeLightPath.bl_description:
Retrieve the type of incoming ray for which the shader is being executed.
Typically used for non-physically-based tricks

ShaderNodeMapRange.name: Map Range
ShaderNodeMapRange.bl_description: Remap a value from a range to a target range

ShaderNodeMapping.name: Mapping
ShaderNodeMapping.bl_description: Transform the input vector by applying translation, rotation, and scale

ShaderNodeMixShader.name: Mix Shader
ShaderNodeMixShader.bl_description: Mix two shaders together. Typically used for material layering

ShaderNodeNewGeometry.name: Geometry
ShaderNodeNewGeometry.bl_description: Retrieve geometric information about the current shading point

ShaderNodeNormal.name: Normal
ShaderNodeNormal.bl_description: Generate a normal vector and a dot product

ShaderNodeNormalMap.name: Normal Map
ShaderNodeNormalMap.bl_description: Generate a perturbed normal from an RGB normal map image. Typically used for faking highly detailed surfaces

ShaderNodeObjectInfo.name: Object Info
ShaderNodeObjectInfo.bl_description: Retrieve information about the object instance

ShaderNodeOutputAOV.name: AOV Output
ShaderNodeOutputAOV.bl_description:
Arbitrary Output Variables.
Provide custom render passes for arbitrary shader node outputs

ShaderNodeOutputLight.name: Light Output
ShaderNodeOutputLight.bl_description: Output light information to a light object

ShaderNodeOutputLineStyle.name: Line Style Output
ShaderNodeOutputLineStyle.bl_description: Control the mixing of texture information into the base color of line styles

ShaderNodeOutputMaterial.name: Material Output
ShaderNodeOutputMaterial.bl_description: Output surface material information for use in rendering

ShaderNodeOutputWorld.name: World Output
ShaderNodeOutputWorld.bl_description: Output light color information to the scene's World

ShaderNodeParticleInfo.name: Particle Info
ShaderNodeParticleInfo.bl_description: Retrieve the data of the particle that spawned the object instance, for example to give variation to multiple instances of an object

ShaderNodePointInfo.name: Point Info
ShaderNodePointInfo.bl_description: Retrieve information about points in a point cloud

ShaderNodeRGBCurve.name: RGB Curves
ShaderNodeRGBCurve.bl_description: Apply color corrections for each color channel

ShaderNodeRGBToBW.name: RGB to BW
ShaderNodeRGBToBW.bl_description: Convert a color's luminance to a grayscale value

ShaderNodeRadialTiling.name: Radial Tiling
ShaderNodeRadialTiling.bl_description: Transform Coordinate System for Radial Tiling

ShaderNodeScript.name: Script
ShaderNodeScript.bl_description:
Generate an OSL shader from a file or text data-block.
Note: OSL shaders are not supported on all GPU backends

ShaderNodeSeparateColor.name: Separate Color
ShaderNodeSeparateColor.bl_description: Split a color into its individual components using multiple models

ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ.name: Separate XYZ
ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ.bl_description: Split a vector into its X, Y, and Z components

ShaderNodeShaderToRGB.name: Shader to RGB
ShaderNodeShaderToRGB.bl_description:
Convert rendering effect (such as light and shadow) to color. Typically used for non-photorealistic rendering, to apply additional effects on the output of BSDFs.
Note: only supported in EEVEE

ShaderNodeSubsurfaceScattering.name: Subsurface Scattering
ShaderNodeSubsurfaceScattering.bl_description:
Subsurface multiple scattering shader to simulate light entering the surface and bouncing internally.
Typically used for materials such as skin, wax, marble or milk

ShaderNodeTangent.name: Tangent
ShaderNodeTangent.bl_description: Generate a tangent direction for the Anisotropic BSDF

ShaderNodeTexBrick.name: Brick Texture
ShaderNodeTexBrick.bl_description: Generate a procedural texture producing bricks

ShaderNodeTexCoord.name: Texture Coordinate
ShaderNodeTexCoord.bl_description:
Retrieve multiple types of texture coordinates.
Typically used as inputs for texture nodes

ShaderNodeTexEnvironment.name: Environment Texture
ShaderNodeTexEnvironment.bl_description: Sample an image file as an environment texture. Typically used to light the scene with the background node

ShaderNodeTexGradient.name: Gradient Texture
ShaderNodeTexGradient.bl_description: Generate interpolated color and intensity values based on the input vector

ShaderNodeTexIES.name: IES Texture
ShaderNodeTexIES.bl_description: Match real world lights with IES files, which store the directional intensity distribution of light sources

ShaderNodeTexImage.name: Image Texture
ShaderNodeTexImage.bl_description: Sample an image file as a texture

ShaderNodeTexVoronoi.name: Voronoi Texture
ShaderNodeTexVoronoi.bl_description: Generate Worley noise based on the distance to random points. Typically used to generate textures such as stones, water, or biological cells

ShaderNodeTexWave.name: Wave Texture
ShaderNodeTexWave.bl_description: Generate procedural bands or rings with noise

ShaderNodeTexWhiteNoise.name: White Noise Texture
ShaderNodeTexWhiteNoise.bl_description: Calculate a random value or color based on an input seed

ShaderNodeUVAlongStroke.name: UV Along Stroke
ShaderNodeUVAlongStroke.bl_description: UV coordinates that map a texture along the stroke length

ShaderNodeUVMap.name: UV Map
ShaderNodeUVMap.bl_description: Retrieve a UV map from the geometry, or the default fallback if none is specified

ShaderNodeValToRGB.name: Color Ramp
ShaderNodeValToRGB.bl_description: Map values to colors with the use of a gradient

ShaderNodeValue.name: Value
ShaderNodeValue.bl_description: Input numerical values to other nodes in the tree

ShaderNodeVectorCurve.name: Vector Curves
ShaderNodeVectorCurve.bl_description: Map input vector components with curves

ShaderNodeVectorDisplacement.name: Vector Displacement
ShaderNodeVectorDisplacement.bl_description: Displace the surface along an arbitrary direction

ShaderNodeVectorRotate.name: Vector Rotate
ShaderNodeVectorRotate.bl_description: Rotate a vector around a pivot point (center)

ShaderNodeVectorTransform.name: Vector Transform
ShaderNodeVectorTransform.bl_description: Convert a vector, point, or normal between world, camera, and object coordinate space

ShaderNodeVertexColor.name: Color Attribute
ShaderNodeVertexColor.bl_description: Retrieve a color attribute, or the default fallback if none is specified

ShaderNodeVolumeAbsorption.name: Volume Absorption
ShaderNodeVolumeAbsorption.bl_description: Absorb light as it passes through the volume

ShaderNodeVolumeCoefficients.name: Volume Coefficients
ShaderNodeVolumeCoefficients.bl_description: Model all three physical processes in a volume, represented by their coefficients

ShaderNodeVolumeInfo.name: Volume Info
ShaderNodeVolumeInfo.bl_description: Read volume data attributes from volume grids

ShaderNodeVolumePrincipled.name: Principled Volume
ShaderNodeVolumePrincipled.bl_description: Combine all volume shading components into a single easy to use node

ShaderNodeVolumeScatter.name: Volume Scatter
ShaderNodeVolumeScatter.bl_description: Scatter light as it passes through the volume, often used to add fog to a scene

ShaderNodeWavelength.name: Wavelength
ShaderNodeWavelength.bl_description: Convert a wavelength value to an RGB value

ShaderNodeWireframe.name: Wireframe
ShaderNodeWireframe.bl_description:
Retrieve the edges of an object as it appears to Cycles.
Note: as meshes are triangulated before being processed by Cycles, topology will always appear triangulated
